items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I worked with a little group in Holland called Ted Easton's band

ctx.x: the case may be, if my health holds out, I can look forward to a busy life of playing. I want to cut my work down to about six months a year, because I don't want to get sick. My health has been excellent and I want to just do this work, and we're booked up, practically two years ahead.

When I say booked up, we don't have signed contracts for that, but we're signed up six months but we know that the work is there, because we keep -- I have turned down a tremendous amount of work which now I will have to do, and I don't mean again to boast or anything, but I have picked up a tremendous amount of publicity here. I do -- you see, they have radio shows over here now that they pay for, that is, in Holland, and Germany and Switzerland and television is quite a bit thing, you pay quite a sum of money…

There is so much work in Holland alone and in Switzerland and in Germany. Germany has 300 jazz clubs, so I say, if I am alive ten years from now, I can be playing these, because I don't have to work hard. I go in, there's a group set up, a trio or quartet or whatever, and they go out and they play about 45 minutes and then they bring me on and I do a half hour, and I do that twice a night.
